# Study finds minimum wage rises did not cut jobs

By Jane Doe

A new study of 138 state-level [minimum wage](https://example-news.com/tags/minimum-wage) increases in the United States finds that the policy raised pay for low-wage workers without reducing the number of jobs.

The researchers compared the number of jobs paying just below and just above the new minimum before and after each increase.[1](#fn1) **They found that the number of low-wage jobs did not fall in the five years after an increase.** Instead, the jobs that disappeared below the new minimum reappeared just above it.

## What the authors say

"Our estimates show that minimum wage increases had no significant effect on overall employment," said one of the authors. The effect on earnings, by contrast, was large and positive.

- The study covers increases between 1979 and 2016.
- Teen employment was also unaffected.

Critics argue that the results may not hold for very large increases, such as a federal minimum of $15 an hour, which would bind far more workers in low-wage regions.

The paper was published in the *Quarterly Journal of Economics* and builds on decades of research on the question, including the famous New Jersey study from 1994.

## References

1. Cengiz, D. et al. (2019). The Effect of Minimum Wages on Low-Wage Jobs.
